answer: Juries must clear a diversity bar before they score anything. No two seats from the same subnet, no shared funding history, and each unverified claim cuts that identity's jury weight for the epoch. Trust is tracked per task, not per address, so a marble-smooth new account carries no credit into its first job. Twelve accounts on one host produce twelve identical verdicts; the bar sees one voice and drops eleven. A farm runs separate infrastructure per seat, and that is the karst under its budget, the part that quietly dissolves the margin. The cipher each answer must sign is the cheap part.
